Public Comment: The public is encouraged to address the Housing Authority on any matter listed on the agenda or on any other matter
within its jurisdiction subject to the rules of decorum described in Section 2.08.020 of the Norwalk Municipal Code. If you wish to address
the Housing Authority, please complete the card that is provided at the rear entrance to Council Chambers and hand the card to the
Sergeant at Arms. The Housing Authority will hear public comment on items listed on the agenda during discussion of the matter and
prior to a vote. The Housing Authority will hear public comment on matters not listed on the agenda during the Oral Communications
period.

Pursuant to provisions of the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the agenda, or unless certain emergency
or special circumstances exist. The Housing Authority may direct staff to investigate and/or schedule certain matters for consideration
at a future Housing Authority meeting.

Please adhere to the following procedures when addressing the Housing Authority:
  ♦ Comments should be limited to 3 minutes or less.
  ♦ Comments should be directed to the Housing Authority as a whole and not directed to individual Commissioners.

Americans with Disabilities Act: In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in a City meeting or other
services offered by this City, please contact the City Clerk’s office, (562) 929-5720. Assisted listening devices are available at this
meeting. Ask the City Clerk if you desire to use this device. Upon request, the agenda and documents in the agenda packet can be
made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability. Notification of at least 48 hours prior to the meeting or time
when services are needed will assist the City staff in assuring that reasonable arrangements can be made to provide accessibility to the
meeting or service.

Note: Any writings and/or documents provided to a majority of the Housing Authority regarding any item on this agenda after it has been
posted will also be made available for public inspection.

Writings and/or documents are available for inspection in the City Clerk’s Department, City Hall, 12700 Norwalk Boulevard during regular
business hours, 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., Monday – Thursday and 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., every other Friday; telephone (562) 929-5720.
You may also contact the City Clerk via e-mail at recordsrequests@norwalkca.gov.

SUBJECT: HOUSING ASSISTANCE PAYMENTS PROGRAM  –  APPROVE
  WARRANT RUN JULY 15, 2019 – AUGUST 1, 2019

Background:

The Housing Authority made payments during the period of July 15, 2019 through
August 1, 2019 for a grand total $596,232.73.

Fiscal Impact: N/A

Citizens Advised: N/A

Strategic Action Plan Implementation: N/A

Recommended Action:

Staff recommends the Housing Authority approve Check Nos. 66752 - 66753 & 213220 -
213224 reported on July 15, 2019 for a total of $5,891.00 and Check Nos. 66754 - 66778
& 213225 - 213381 reported on August 1, 2019 for a total of $590,341.73.

Attachments:

1. Check Summary Information Sheet
2. Check Summary
   ATTACHMENT 1
  Housing Authority
  Check Summary Information Sheet

The warrants in the Housing Authority agenda report are for housing assistance payments
made under the Section 8 Housing Choice Voucher program. The payee has a choice of
receiving the housing assistance payment via direct deposit, which is an electronic fund
transfer made directly to the payee’s bank account, or by paper check.

In the check summary report, the direct deposits are listed first as direct deposits, and then
the checks follow. Each direct deposit and paper check represents payment for 1 to 20
tenants depending upon the number of Section 8 tenants the payee has.

The payee is the property owner or designated management company. The property owner
or manager may be a corporation, partnership, trust, or individual. The payee name is the
owner or manager’s legal business or individual name, which must match Internal Revenue
Service (IRS) records. Here are some common abbreviations used in business names:

LLC = Limited Liability Company

LP = Limited Partnership

DBA = “Doing Business As”

LTD = Limited

Checks made out to the City of Norwalk Housing Authority represent the Family Self
Sufficiency (FSS) escrow deposits. These checks are deposited into the Housing Authority’s
bank account where the funds earn interest and are kept in escrow until the FSS participant
successfully completes the program at which time they receive the balance of their account.

Norwalk Housing Investors, LP is the owner of Center Pointe Villas at 14100 San Antonio
and 11856 Orange. Payments are for Section 8 participants living in these buildings.

Payments to housing authorities, such as the Orange County Housing Authority and San
Bernardino County Housing, represent reimbursements for our participants who have
transferred to those jurisdictions under portability.

Please call Kristin Maithonis at ext. 5653 if you have any questions.

SUBJECT: RESOLUTION  NO.  NHA-157  -  DESTRUCTION  OF  OBSOLETE
  RECORDS

Background:

State law provides that certain City records, which are not required for legal or legislative
purposes, may be destroyed after two years. In addition, on February 17, 2009, City
Council adopted Resolution No. 09-05 establishing a records retention schedule for City
records. Attached is a list of obsolete records submitted by the Housing division that may
be destroyed pursuant to State law and the City’s adopted retention schedule. The
Authority Counsel has reviewed the list and approved destruction.

Fiscal Impact: N/A

Citizens Advised: N/A

Strategic Action Plan Implementation: N/A

Recommended Action:

Staff recommends the Housing Authority adopt Resolution No. NHA-157, A
RESOLUTION OF THE CITY OF NORWALK HOUSING AUTHORITY AUTHORIZING
THE DESTRUCTION OF CERTAIN RECORDS IN THE HOUSING DIVISION OF THE
COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT DEPARTMENT.

Attachments:

1. Resolution No. NHA-157
2. Department Head Approval form with Authority to Destroy form.
   Attachment No. 1
  RESOLUTION NO. NHA-157

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY OF NORWALK HOUSING AUTHORITY
  AUTHORIZING THE DESTRUCTION OF CERTAIN RECORDS IN THE
  HOUSING DIVISION OF THE COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT
  DEPARTMENT

  WHEREAS, Section 34090 of the Government Code provides for the destruction
of public records more than two years old with the consent of the Department Head and
the approval of the City Attorney and legislative body by resolution; and

  WHEREAS, the City Council adopted Resolution No. 09-05 on February 17, 2009
establishing a Records Retention Schedule, which identified City records and established
their retention.

  NOW, THEREFORE, THE CITY OF NORWALK HOUSING AUTHORITY DOES
HEREBY RESOLVE, DETERMINE AND ORDER AS FOLLOWS:

  Section 1. In accordance with the City’s adopted Records Retention Schedule
and Government Code §34090, the following identified records are no longer required:

    Inactive Section 8 Case applications (not placed/ineligible) – through
  June 30, 2016
    Financial Records – through June 30, 2012
    Section 8 Administrative Plan – Superceded February 15, 2011
    Administrative Reports required by HUD – through June 30, 2012
  Section 2. Pursuant to the approval of Authority Counsel, the Housing Authority
does hereby authorize the destruction of said records from the Housing Division.

  Section 3. The Housing Authority hereby finds and determines that said
aforementioned records are more than two years old and/or no longer required nor are
the same required to be kept by statute or law.

  Section 4. The Clerk is hereby directed to cause said records to be destroyed
in accordance with the terms and conditions of section 34090 of the government Code of
the State of California.

  Section 5. That upon destruction of the identified records, the City Clerk’s
Department shall make a certification of destruction of such records and file the original
of same in the office of the City Clerk.
   APPROVED AND ADOPTED on this 20th day of August 2019.

  _______________________________
  MARGARITA L. RIOS
  CHAIR

SUBJECT: RESOLUTION NO. NHA-158 - AUTHORIZES THE FILING OF AN
  APPLICATION TO THE UNITED STATES DEPARTMENT OF HOUSING
  AND URBAN DEVELOPMENT FOR THE MAINSTREAM VOUCHER
  PROGRAM AND AUTHORIZING THE EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR TO
  EXECUTE ANY REQUIRED AGREEMENTS

Background:

The Housing Authority currently administers 705 Housing Choice Vouchers for very low-
income households through funding provided by the United States Department of
Housing and Urban Development (HUD). The program delivers rental assistance to help
eligible, very low-income residents afford to rent units in the private market.

On July 2, 2019, HUD announced a Notice of Funding Availability (NOFA) for Mainstream
Vouchers, and the application due date is September 5, 2019. Mainstream Vouchers are
for non-elderly persons with disabilities. The purpose of the vouchers is to further the
goals of the Olmstead Act, which held that public entities must provide community-based
services to persons with disabilities when (1) such services are appropriate; (2) the
affected persons do not oppose community-based treatment; and (3) community-based
services can be reasonably accommodated, taking into account the resources available
to the public entity and the needs of others who are receiving disability services from the
entity.

The NOFA provides funding for the Housing Assistance Payment and administrative
costs associated with the additional vouchers. The funding application is competitive and
points are awarded based upon an applicant’s prior experience assisting persons with
disabilities, admissions preferences, partnerships, and program evaluation.
 Housing Authority  August 20, 2019
Resolution No. NHA-158 – Mainstream Vouchers  Page No. 2

Under the NOFA, public housing authorities (PHA) are awarded points if the PHA targets
vouchers to assist non-elderly disabled applicants who are:

  •  Transitioning out of institutional and other segregated settings;
  •  At serious risk of institutionalization;
  •  Currently experiencing homelessness;
  •  Previously experienced homelessness and a current client in a permanent
  supportive housing or rapid rehousing project; or
  •  At risk of experiencing homelessness.

To ensure that the most vulnerable residents are assisted, staff recommends that all five
(5) preference categories listed above be adopted. The NOFA requires that the Housing
Authority amend its waiting list preferences within six (6) months of the award date if any
special admission preferences will be utilized. The admission preferences can be limited
to a certain number of applicants, as long as the number is sufficient to reach program
utilization goals.

The NOFA also provides points to PHAs who provide or obtain supportive services for
program participants. However, the NOFA does not provide funding for the provision of
additional services. The City has partnerships with Home Ownership for Personal
Empowerment (HOPE) through the HOME Investment Partnerships Program and
Kingdom Causes Bellflower (KCB) through the City’s Homeless Prevention and Rapid
Rehousing Program and the Housing Authority’s homeless voucher preference. With
these partnerships, additional services available at the Harbor Regional Center (HRC)
and Los Angeles County Department of Health Services (DHS) are leveraged to provide
supportive services through our existing programs.

KCB, HOPE, DHS and HRC have indicated that they will provide letters of intent to
provide at least one of the following services to the Mainstream Voucher Program:

  •  Outreach and referral of persons currently experiencing homelessness and/or at
  risk of homelessness;
  •  Housing navigation/ADA modifications;
  •  Moving assistance; and/or
  •  Referring, coordinating or providing home and community-based services.

If the Housing Authority receives a Mainstream Voucher award through the NOFA, the
partner organizations will enter into an agreement for services with the Housing Authority
and utilize their existing funding and resources to provide the necessary supportive
services.
 Housing Authority  August 20, 2019
Resolution No. NHA-158 – Mainstream Vouchers  Page No. 3

Staff is still analyzing the number of Mainstream Vouchers that could be supported and
utilized within twelve (12) months of receiving an award, and is recommending that the
Housing Authority apply for up to twenty (20) Mainstream Vouchers.

Applying for additional rental vouchers is one of the goals contained in the Housing
Authority’s adopted 5-Year Public Housing Agency Plan. Additional vouchers targeting
homeless persons and individuals at risk of homelessness will support the City’s effort in
preventing and combatting homelessness.

Fiscal Impact: N/A

Citizens Advised: N/A

Strategic Action Plan Implementation:

The recommended action will further the City’s strategic plan goal of: (2.A.1) Actively
seeking and applying for grants to support City programs and projects.

Recommended Action:

Staff recommends the Housing Authority adopt Resolution No. NHA-158, A
RESOLUTION OF THE CITY OF NORWALK HOUSING AUTHORITY AUTHORIZING
THE FILING OF AN APPLICATION TO THE UNITED STATES DEPARTMENT OF
HOUSING AND URBAN DEVELOPMENT FOR THE MAINSTREAM VOUCHER
PROGRAM AND AUTHORIZING THE EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR TO EXECUTE ANY
REQUIRED AGREEMENTS.

Attachments:

Resolution No. NHA-158
   RESOLUTION NO. NHA-158

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY OF NORWALK HOUSING AUTHORITY
  AUTHORIZING THE FILING OF AN APPLICATION TO THE UNITED
  STATES DEPARTMENT OF HOUSING AND URBAN DEVELOPMENT
  FOR THE MAINSTREAM VOUCHER PROGRAM AND AUTHORIZING
  THE EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR TO EXECUTE ANY REQUIRED
  AGREEMENTS

  WHEREAS, funds are being made available under the United States Department
of Housing and Urban Development Notice of Funding Availability (FR-6300-N-43) for the
Mainstream Vouchers Program; and

  WHEREAS, the City of Norwalk Housing Authority, being established in
accordance with Section 34290 et.seq., of the California Health and Safety Code, is
administering the Housing Choice Voucher Program and is eligible to apply under the
Notice of Funding Availability; and

  WHEREAS, applying for additional rental vouchers is a goal contained within City
of Norwalk Housing Authority’s Five-Year Public Housing Agency Plan for 2015-2020
adopted on February 17, 2015; and

  WHEREAS, the City of Norwalk Housing Authority has determined that there is a
need for Mainstream Vouchers to assist non-elderly disabled individuals and households;
and

  WHEREAS, if funding is awarded under the Mainstream Voucher Program, the
City of Norwalk Housing Authority will amend the Administrative Plan waiting list
preferences to align with the preferences stated in the application for funding.

  NOW, THEREFORE, THE CITY OF NORWALK HOUSING AUTHORITY
HEREBY DETERMINES, FINDS, AND RESOLVES AS FOLLOWS:

  Section 1. That staff prepare an application and relevant documentation to the
United States Department of Housing and Urban Development for Mainstream Vouchers.

  Section 2. That the Executive Director or his designee is authorized to execute
and submit the application and documentation by the application deadline of
September 5, 2019.

  Section 3. That the Executive Director is authorized to execute any required
agreements related to the Mainstream Voucher application, funding award and program
implementation.
   APPROVED AND ADOPTED on this 20th day of August 2019.
